title: Shemot: these are the names (Exodus 1:1)
hookLine: the book begins by naming those who went down to Egypt

lines: A BOOK THAT STARTS WITH NAMES.
cards: A new manager gets your name wrong. So does a teacher with thirty kids, and a cousin at a wedding. It's small, and it can sting anyway.
Then there's the opposite: someone you met once, months ago, says your name without hesitating. That one lands.
The second book of the Torah, the one about slavery and freedom, could start with a king or a plague or a burning bush. It starts with a list of names.

teach.h: EXODUS IN GREEK, SHEMOT IN HEBREW.
teach.b: In English this book is Exodus, from the Greek for going out.
In Hebrew, like the other books of the Torah, it's named for an early word: Shemot. Names.

The first verse, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt with Jacob." Then the list: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, and the rest.
This puzzled the rabbis. Genesis already gave the names of everyone who went down to Egypt, not long before. Why repeat it?
Rashi answers with a picture. The prophet Isaiah says God brings out the stars by number and calls each one by name.
The Torah counts these people again, Rashi says, the way you'd count something precious, and names them to show how dear they are.

teach.h: A KING WHO KNEW NOT JOSEPH.
teach.b: A few verses later comes a chilling line: "Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph." A ruler who doesn't know the name. That's how the slavery starts.
Then two midwives refuse Pharaoh's order to kill the baby boys, and the text gives their names: Shiphrah and Puah. The king of Egypt?
In the whole story, he never gets a name. He's only Pharaoh, a title. The powerful man stays anonymous, and the two brave women are remembered by name.
Before the story of freedom, the book stops to say who these people were.

how: In synagogues, Shemot begins the winter stretch of Exodus readings; each Hebrew book of the Torah is named for an early word, so Genesis is Bereshit, in the beginning, and Exodus is Shemot, names.

games.q: you're writing the opening of the story of slavery and freedom. how do you begin?
o: with the names of the family who came down to Egypt.
with the baby in the basket.
games.why: the book begins: these are the names of the sons of Israel. the new king who knew not Joseph comes a few verses later.

practice: Picture someone you see often but can't name: the barista, the security guard, the neighbor in the hallway, the parent at pickup, a coworker on another floor.
See their face clearly, and settle that next time you'll ask, and use the name once, right away, so it sticks.
